text:
Five games is all Marco Kasper has played this season, so there isn't much of a season to judge. What's there is encouraging: one goal, 15 minutes a night, and the Red Wings taking 66% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five. That number will move a lot in a sample this small.

Detroit's coverage has been about what comes next. NHL.com ran the headline "'He looks confident and strong right now': Kasper back at full strength for Red Wings," and Sports Illustrated's read was "Red Wings Get Much-Needed Boost From Marco Kasper as McLellan Weighs Bigger Role."

The 8th overall pick of 2022 needs it to go well. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season (-0.3 wins), and NHL EDGE ranks his skating and shot speed low among forwards. His best trait last season, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, was getting to the net: 6.1 chances per 60 from the home-plate area, 80th percentile among forwards. Watch his ice time over the next few weeks; that's where the bigger role would show first.
